previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic pain, GERD, CHF with preserved ejection fraction, and recurrent VTE on warfarin presented with one week of progressive diffuse abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had recently run out of pantoprazole. Evaluation revealed enteritis on CT abdomen and a urinary tract infection on urinalysis. She was treated with Bactrim and Flagyl for both infections, restarted on pantoprazole, and had her warfarin dose reduced to 1 mg daily due to antibiotic interaction. Her heart failure was managed with continued diuretic therapy. Symptoms improved during the 2-day stay, and she was discharged home on a short course of antibiotics, pantoprazole, adjusted warfarin, and modified furosemide dosing, with instructions to follow up for INR monitoring.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis

Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
